newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia mulls selling 25 pct of state telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Croatia mulls selling 25 pct of state telecoms.

text.p: Croatia could sell upto 25 percent of state telecom monopoly HPT to private investors to raise money for the reconstruction of the war-damaged town of Vukovar, a government minister said.

Privatisation Minister Ivan Penic declined to provide a precise timetable but said a high-level political decision had been made to go ahead with privatising parts of larger state-owned enterprises and utilities, including the postal service and the telecommunications sector.

"One proposal we are working on is to sell up to 25 percent of the HPT through an international tender and use the money -- between $600 million and $1 billion -- to rebuild Vukovar," Penic told Reuters in an interview.
The Danube harbour town in the far east of Croatia was almost completely destroyed during a three-month siege by the Yugoslav army that ended in Vukovar's surrender five years ago.
The region, still under control of rebel Serbs, is supposed to be "peacefully reintegrated" with the rest of the country by June next year.
HPT is the most lucrative Croatian company with some 331.8 million kuna ($61 million) net profit in 1995.
It has grown strongly over the past few years, doubling the number of telephone lines in the country since 1990.
Penic said the government was thinking about splitting the post and telecommunications departments before the proposed sell-off.
"We are looking right now into various privatisation models of telecoms in Europe, and will come up with the solution which is the best for us," he added.

Croatia's parliament will have to pass a special bill for the privatisation of each of the country's seven large utilities and state-owned firms that have been earmarked for restructuring over the next few years.

The first in line is loss-making state oil company INA (Industrija Nafte) which accounts for one eighth of the output of the Croatian economy. Penic said INA could start selling its non-core assets in the next few months.
"We would like to start with the restructuring of INA in the first few months of the next year," Penic said.
